text:
maria_support: Heads up — customer reported a 502 + unexpected billing spike on /v1/generate. They provided a client-side id only: client_request_id=8f3a2b7e-e3d1-4c9a. Timeframe: 2026-03-15 14:20-14:25 UTC. I tried Kibana search and nothing with that id. Can infra/eng help with a server-side lookup and retention guidance?

dylan_infra: On it. Which customer/org?

maria_support: Acme Health (org: acme-health, acct id: acct_0A1B). They also reported a couple intermittent 401s earlier.

priya_eng: If the customer only provides a client-generated GUID we often can't find it unless it was forwarded in a header or body that we index. Ask them for response headers (curl -v) or a debug bundle. I'll try broad searches by src ip + path too.

maria_support: Their curl (redacted):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-...REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello","client_request_id":"8f3a2b7e-e3d1-4c9a"}'
```
They said response was a 502 with an HTML-ish body and no x-rw-req header.

dylan_infra: OK. I'll run KQL over that window. Try queries in Kibana like:
```
request.path: "/v1/generate" and http.response.status: 502 and client_request_id: "8f3a2b7e-e3d1-4c9a"
```
If empty, also try header variants: `http.request.headers.client_request_id: "8f3a2b7e-e3d1-4c9a"`. Expand time range with `@timestamp: [2026-03-15T14:15:00 TO 2026-03-15T14:30:00]` style.

priya_eng: FYI retention: hot logs are 21 days, cold archive is 180 days. If this was >21 days ago we'll need a cold retrieval (support ticket with timeframe + impact).

alex_ops: I found a match using src IP and path (no client id). Matched trace id: trace-0b7c9df. Log line:```
2026-03-15T14:22:17Z INFO request_id=trace-0b7c9df path=/v1/generate upstream=embedder-2 status=502 error=\"timeout waiting for model\"
```

maria_support: Awesome. Customer is asking for repro steps — should we request a debug bundle? Also should we proactively offer a credit?

priya_eng: Ask them for `curl -v` to capture response headers (we need x-rw-req / x-rw-trace if present). If they can run our debug bundle endpoint, include approximate timestamp and any trace ids they have. Example instruction for customer: 
```
# run verbose curl to capture headers
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-...' -d '{"prompt":"...","client_request_id":"8f3a2b7e-e3d1-4c9a"}'
```
If they can't repro, offer a one-time credit and open an internal investigation. We already have a trace id (trace-0b7c9df) so ask them to upload the bundle and reference that.

maria_support: @priya_eng do we need eng-oncall to triage embedder-2? @dylan_infra any node events at that time? :thinking_face:

dylan_infra: Checked node metrics: embedder-2 OOM at 14:21:59, restarted and came back at 14:22:14; backlog spike between 14:21:50-14:22:30. That aligns with the timeout. I'll open an incident and mark for capacity/autoscale review. Short term: recommend customer retry with smaller prompt length. Long term: autoscale tweak.

support-bot: ticket #INC-2581 created: Investigate embedder-2 OOM and customer 502s. Assigned to @dylan_infra.

maria_support: Thanks — I'll reply to the customer asking for `curl -v` output and offering a credit. I'll include the trace id we found (trace-0b7c9df) so they can reference it in a debug bundle upload.

alex_ops: Also note: if logs needed are older than 21 days, we can pull from cold archive but it takes ~48 hours and requires exact time windows. Mention that to the customer if they ask.
